To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the concept of distributed heredity is useful to describe the continuity of inheritance and ontogenetic processes and that (ii) the informational heterarchy of these processes is not reducible to a hierarchical description of the processes.
the continuity between genetic, epigenomic and microbiotic inheritance and ontogenetic processes is best explained by a heterarchical, process-oriented approach.
the nature of biological systems is best understood by a heterarchical approach to biological systems, which is a non-hierarchical approach to the organization of processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the processes of inheritance and development, which are the result of complex interactions of genetic, epigentic, and microbiotic information.
the nature of complex biological systems, and in particular, with their capacity for self-organization, self-maintenance and development.
the nature of the processes that are involved in the production of phenotypes, and the nature of the information that is involved in the process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

inheritance and development are heterarchical processes, which are characterized by the continuous exchange of information and the continuous reorganization of the whole system, which is not reducible to any single component.
the biological processes of inheritance and ontogenetic development are heterarchical and distributed.
the nature of inheritance and development are heterarchical and that the hierarchical perspective is insufficient to grasp their nature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

biological inheritance is a process that is distributed over time and space and that is heterarchically integrated in a complex network of processes that includes the genetic, epigenetics, microbiotic and environmental levels.
the heterarchical perspective is a necessary tool in order to understand the complex and dynamic nature of the processes that constitute inheritance and development.
the nature of biological systems is not reducible to a single level of organization and that biological systems are not reducible either to their components, nor to the whole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heterarchical perspective is a more adequate way to conceptualise inheritance and development.
the nature of biological systems is not hierarchical and that biological processes are better described as distributed, heterarchical and dynamic.

biological systems are not organized in a linear, top-down manner, and that the idea of a single, hierarchical level of description is not adequate to explain the complex and integrated processuality of biological systems.
